new_entities.name: Apple cider vinegar
new_entities.description: Apple cider vinegar or closely related meal-time vinegar interventions used to blunt glycaemic response to carbohydrate-rich meals.

new_entities.name: Postprandial glycaemia
new_entities.description: Short-term blood glucose excursion, peak glucose, or glucose area under the curve after a meal.

edges.effect_quant: A 2017 meta-analysis of meal-time vinegar trials found lower postprandial glucose AUC with vinegar than control, and a 2020 crossover rice-meal study in 15 healthy women cut 0-120 minute incremental glucose AUC by 42.4% when vinegar-soaked dried apple was co-ingested. Chronic vinegar trials also improve fasting glycaemia, but the cleanest evidence is still the acute post-meal signal.
edges.population: healthy adults or adults with impaired glycaemic control consuming vinegar with carbohydrate-containing meals or daily over weeks
edges.mechanism: Acetic acid likely slows gastric emptying and dampens early starch digestion, reducing the speed at which glucose from a meal reaches the bloodstream.
edges.summary: Apple cider vinegar has a real acute glycaemic edge, but it is narrower than supplement marketing suggests. The literature supports a modest reduction in post-meal glucose excursions when vinegar is taken with starchy meals, while chronic benefits are less uniform and depend on the population studied.
edges.caveats: Most trials use small samples, mixed vinegar types, and controlled test meals rather than everyday eating patterns. This edge is about short-term glycaemic response, not proof that vinegar meaningfully treats diabetes on its own.

evidence.citation: ShishehborF et al 2017 Diabetes Res Clin Pract
evidence.notes: Vinegar consumption can attenuate postprandial glucose and insulin responses; a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials.
Co-ingested vinegar-soaked or preloaded dried apple mitigated acute postprandial glycemia of rice meal in healthy subjects under equicarbohydrate conditions.

effect_quant.comparator: incremental glucose AUC0-120 versus rice reference meal

evidence.notes: Daily red wine vinegar ingestion for eight weeks improves glucose homeostasis and affects the metabolome but does not reduce adiposity in adults.

effect_quant.comparator: change in insulin resistance in vinegar group over 8 weeks
